newsitem.title: UK: Intertanko to launch tanker position database.
newsitem.headline: Intertanko to launch tanker position database.

text.p: Data on the whereabouts and availability of oil tankers will be published from next year on a restricted Internet-based service, a tanker owner involved in the project said on Thursday.

"We finally go live on January 1," said Bruce Ogilvy, managing director of Stelmar tankers and contributor to the project being set up by the International Association of Independent Tanker Owners (Intertanko).

The information will be supplied by various tanker owners and be supplemented by four selected brokers, and may be used by tanker owners as well as charterers to obtain more transparent information on tonnage availability.
"On a global basis tanker ownership is fragmented and in the spot market the lack of good-quality ship information puts the shipowner at a disadvantage," Intertanko said in an open letter.
"This information gap tends to distort free competition and shift the balance of power to the strongest player in the market -- the charterer."
The first six-month phase of the project will focus on refined oil product carriers of between 29,000 and 49,000 deadweight tonnes in the Caribbean-Atlantic markets, and in Asia.
"A number of owners have already agreed to participate...It is in their interests to do so," Ogilvy told journalists at an Intertanko meeting in London.
"The service will be monitored to see if anybody is putting in misinformation...The idea is to build up trust for this initial stage, and then we hope to expand the service."
"It will be restricted to the participants in the project on a restricted and confidential basis."
Ogilvy added that additional information, such as the dimensions of each vessel, would also be accessible behind the main Internet screens.
